l4_steps.name: Capture and validate sourcing requirement
l4_steps.input: Purchase requisition or strategic sourcing request from business unit
l4_steps.output: Validated sourcing request with spend category code and business justification
l4_steps.kpi: Sourcing request processed within 2 business days of submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines carry highly fragmented procurement across MRO, IT, fuel, catering, and ground handling — category ownership disputes between Finance and Operations delay sourcing initiation by 3–7 days on average

l4_steps.name: Conduct spend analysis and category benchmarking
l4_steps.system: SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO) + SAP Ariba Analytics
l4_steps.input: Validated sourcing request, historical PO data from SAP S/4HANA
l4_steps.output: Category spend cube, supplier concentration report, year-on-year variance analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Spend data coverage ≥95% of addressable spend in category; analysis completed within 3 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel, MRO, and ground handling spend frequently sits in legacy cost centers not yet mapped to SAP Ariba Analytics, creating data blind spots that understate category spend by up to 20%

l4_steps.name: Assess supply market and regulatory landscape
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Supplier Risk + Dun & Bradstreet Direct+
l4_steps.input: Category spend cube, procurement policy, FAA/DOT regulatory requirements
l4_steps.output: Market assessment report with supplier landscape map and regulatory constraint summary
l4_steps.kpi: Market assessment completed within 5 business days; ≥3 qualified alternative suppliers identified per category
l4_steps.pain_point: Aviation-specific supplier pools (e.g. FAA Part 145 repair stations, EASA-approved MRO shops) are narrow — market power asymmetry severely constrains negotiation leverage; fewer than 3 qualified suppliers in many technical categories

l4_steps.name: Define sourcing strategy and evaluation scorecard
l4_steps.input: Market assessment report, category strategy template, stakeholder requirements
l4_steps.output: Approved sourcing strategy document with weighted evaluation scorecard (technical, commercial, risk)
l4_steps.kpi: Stakeholder sign-off on strategy within 3 business days; evaluation criteria weighted and approved prior to RFx issuance
l4_steps.pain_point: Flight Operations and Maintenance stakeholders frequently bypass procurement to negotiate directly with preferred vendors, undermining competitive process integrity and creating maverick spend exposure

l4_steps.name: Build and issue RFI/RFP/RFQ package to suppliers
l4_steps.input: Sourcing strategy, technical specification from business unit, approved supplier invitation list
l4_steps.output: Published RFx with Q&A forum, supplier NDA, and submission deadline; ≥5 qualified suppliers invited
l4_steps.kpi: RFP issued within 5 business days of strategy approval; minimum 5 qualified suppliers invited per event
l4_steps.pain_point: Aviation technical specifications for avionics components and GSE routinely contain ITAR/EAR export control clauses requiring Legal pre-clearance — this delays RFP issuance by 3–10 business days and is not tracked within standard Ariba Sourcing workflow

l4_steps.name: Manage supplier Q&A period and receive proposals
l4_steps.input: Published RFx, supplier clarification queries, potential addenda
l4_steps.output: Clarification addenda issued to all bidders; sealed supplier proposals received in Ariba
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal submission rate ≥60% of invited suppliers; addenda issued to all bidders within 24 hours of Q&A close
l4_steps.pain_point: RFx deadline extensions to accommodate late supplier queries inflate sourcing cycle time by 5–15 days; SAP Ariba version-lock on RFP documents can prevent late addenda from being distributed to all bidders simultaneously, creating legal exposure

l4_steps.name: Score proposals against weighted evaluation criteria
l4_steps.role: Evaluation Committee (Category Manager, BU Technical Lead, Finance)
l4_steps.input: Sealed supplier proposals, approved evaluation scorecard
l4_steps.output: Ranked vendor shortlist with technical and commercial composite scores
l4_steps.kpi: Scoring completed within 5 business days of proposal deadline; inter-evaluator score variance <15% per criterion
l4_steps.pain_point: Technical evaluators from Flight Operations and MRO departments frequently lack procurement training, producing non-compliant scoring narratives that expose the airline to bid protest risk and require rework cycles

l4_steps.name: Conduct vendor due diligence and financial health check
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Supplier Risk + Dun & Bradstreet Direct+
l4_steps.input: Shortlisted vendor list from scoring output
l4_steps.output: Supplier risk profile covering financial stability, ESG standing, and regulatory compliance status
l4_steps.kpi: Due diligence completed within 3 business days; zero unresolved critical risk flags at award recommendation stage
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-pandemic supply chain fragility means key MRO and GSE suppliers carry elevated debt loads — D&B Paydex scores alone are insufficient for FAA-regulated suppliers, which also require manual verification of current FAA Repair Station Certificate (Form 8310-3) validity

l4_steps.name: Conduct best-and-final-offer (BAFO) round
l4_steps.input: Shortlisted vendors, scoring results, commercial baseline pricing
l4_steps.output: BAFO submissions from shortlisted vendors, updated commercial comparison matrix
l4_steps.kpi: Cost reduction vs. baseline ≥8% for competitive categories; BAFO round completed within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel hedging contracts and aircraft wet-lease negotiations require Treasury and Legal involvement that is not modelled in standard Ariba BAFO workflows — offline negotiation tracks create version control issues and audit trail gaps

l4_steps.name: Prepare award recommendation and obtain DOA approval
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Procurement (Approval workflow) + SAP S/4HANA Finance
l4_steps.input: BAFO results, evaluation summary, Delegation of Authority (DOA) matrix
l4_steps.output: Award recommendation memo with financial impact analysis; spend authority approval obtained per DOA tier
l4_steps.kpi: Approval obtained within 2 business days for contracts within CPO authority; 100% of awards documented against DOA matrix
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-tier DOA matrices mean large MRO or IT contracts frequently require Board-level approval, creating 10–20-day bottlenecks when procurement timeline is driven by AOG (Aircraft on Ground) operational urgency

l4_steps.name: Draft, negotiate, and execute vendor contract
l4_steps.input: Award recommendation, standard contract templates, BAFO final submission
l4_steps.output: Fully executed contract with SLAs, liability caps, termination clauses, and insurance requirements
l4_steps.kpi: Contract execution within 10 business days of award; ≤2 redline round-trips on standard contract terms
l4_steps.pain_point: Aviation-specific indemnity clauses (hull and liability coverage requirements for ground handlers, hangar keepers liability) routinely stall negotiations — the airline's aviation contract template library in SAP Ariba Contracts is often outdated versus current IATA Ground Handling Agreement (IGHA 2013) standards

l4_steps.name: Activate vendor master record in SAP S/4HANA
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Contracts + SAP S/4HANA Finance (Vendor Master)
l4_steps.input: Executed contract with payment terms, banking details, and tax classification
l4_steps.output: Active vendor master record in SAP S/4HANA; contract record linked in SAP Ariba Contracts
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor master activated within 1 business day of contract execution; 100% contract data accuracy confirmed in Ariba Contracts
l4_steps.pain_point: Duplicate vendor master entries in SAP S/4HANA (created by decentralised AP teams across hub stations without central Ariba governance) cause payment routing errors and complicate spend reporting; MDM cleanse required for ~15% of new vendor activations

l4_steps.name: Execute vendor onboarding and EDI/API integration test
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration + EDI/API Gateway
l4_steps.input: Activated vendor master, executed contract, integration specification
l4_steps.output: Completed onboarding checklist; EDI/API test results confirming PO and invoice transaction accuracy
l4_steps.kpi: Onboarding completed within 10 business days of contract activation; EDI transaction error rate <1% in test phase
l4_steps.pain_point: MRO suppliers (FAA Part 145 repair stations) and smaller catering vendors often lack EDI/API capability — manual PO and invoice processing inflates error rate and extends AOG parts procurement lead times by 24–48 hours

l4_steps.name: Establish vendor KPI scorecard and SLA baseline
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Supplier Performance Management + Tableau
l4_steps.input: Executed contract SLAs, historical baseline data where available, operations KPI definitions
l4_steps.output: Published vendor scorecard template; KPI dashboard live in Tableau for operational stakeholder visibility
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor scorecard published within 5 business days of go-live; ≥90% of contracted SLA fields populated at baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: Procurement and Flight Operations use conflicting KPI definitions for vendor performance (procurement measures on-time delivery; Ops measures AOG-free rate) — SAP Ariba SPM module is not configured to capture operations-driven SLAs, requiring manual Tableau overlays that are inconsistently maintained

l4_steps.name: Conduct 90-day post-award performance review
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Supplier Performance Management + Tableau
l4_steps.input: Vendor scorecard, invoice data, delivery records, and incident logs from first 90 days
l4_steps.output: Post-award review report; corrective action plan (CAP) issued if SLA threshold not met
l4_steps.kpi: 90-day review completed on schedule for 100% of strategic vendors; vendor SLA achievement ≥85% at 90-day gate
l4_steps.pain_point: High-volume catering and GSE contracts rarely receive structured 90-day reviews due to Category Manager bandwidth constraints — performance issues compound undetected until contract renewal, entrenching underperforming vendors and increasing switching costs
